To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probability density functions of a Wiener-driven Integrate-and-Fry model and of a random spiking neuron model are related via an integral transform.
the probability densities corresponding to stochastic neuronal models can be related via integral transforms.

(i) the internal and the external variability can be related to each other by integral transforms, (ii) the probability density functions of the corresponding models can be mapped one onto another, (iii) this mapping is not one-to-one and (iv) the mapping can be used to derive the internal variability from the external one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the theoretical connections between different expressions of noise in mathematical neuronal models.
the mathematical formalization and theoretical connections between different neuronal models that correspond to different expressions of the intrinsic and extrinsic noise sources.
a mathematical investigation into the stochastic aspects of neuronal activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the internal variability of a neuron is equivalent to the external variability of an external input to the neuron.
, although they are mathematically different, the two sources of variability are not so far apart as they seem to be.
the mathematical description of internal and external sources of variability is similar, and thus the two can be mapped one onto the other via an appropriate integral transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stochastic models for the internal and external noise can be related via a change of variables.
, although the intrinsic and extrinsic noise sources can be expressed by different mathematical frameworks, they are not so far apart as they seem to be.
the stochastic processes that model intrinsic and extrinsic variability can be mapped to one another via a change of variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the sources of variability are distinct in origin, the mathematical tools to model them are not necessarily different.
the mathematical expressions for the two categories of noise can be mapped to each other via a change of variables, which can be used as a tool for the comparison between models.
the mathematical framework of stochastic models is not as restrictive as it may seem.
